medium.title: Ahead of Market: 10 Things That Will Decide Stock Market Action on Monday
medium.summary:
Indian equity markets closed Friday's session in positive territory, with both the Sensex and Nifty 50 posting gains exceeding 0.3%. The rally was supported by a combination of factors: an easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (reducing risk-off pressure on EMs including INR), diminished expectations of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes (broadly supportive of EM capital inflows and INR stability), progress on the India-Japan bilateral summit (positive for sentiment on FDI/diplomatic flows), and a recovery in the IT sector. For international fund managers, the reduced Fed rate hike expectations are the most macro-relevant takeaway — a more dovish Fed path would support INR through reduced dollar strength and could sustain FPI equity inflows into Indian markets. Watch Monday's opening for follow-through momentum and any further Fed commentary over the weekend.

medium.title: Oil Price Today (July 6): Crude oil extends fall, hovers below $72. Here are 2 major reasons for the decline
medium.summary: Brent crude slipped to $71.88/barrel while WTI eased to $68.58/barrel, extending recent declines. For India — one of the world's largest crude importers — sustained weakness in oil prices is a meaningful macro positive. Lower crude reduces India's import bill, helping narrow the trade deficit and current account deficit (CAD), both of which are key structural pressures on the INR. A softer oil price environment also eases domestic fuel inflation, potentially reducing upward pressure on CPI and giving the RBI additional headroom on monetary policy. INR traders should monitor whether crude stabilizes below $72, as a prolonged stay at these levels could provide modest but meaningful INR support. Bond investors may also take note, as lower oil-driven inflation could reinforce expectations of an accommodative policy stance, supporting G-Sec prices.

medium.title: Oil slips after OPEC+ agrees to raise output targets
medium.summary: OPEC+ has agreed to raise output targets from August, triggering a dip in oil prices as markets price in additional supply. However, analysts caution that actual output increases may be constrained by ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Gulf region. Gulf oil exports in June surged by over 3 million barrels, though they remain below pre-conflict levels, while Russia's crude shipments rose sharply due to domestic refinery disruptions. For INR and Indian macro watchers, the supply-side expansion from OPEC+ — if sustained — reinforces the bearish crude narrative, which is directionally positive for India's external balances. However, geopolitical risk remains a wildcard; any escalation disrupting Strait of Hormuz flows could rapidly reverse the trend and reignite INR depreciation pressures. Watch Russia-India crude trade flows closely, as discounted Russian oil remains a key input for Indian refiners.
